apps.title: django-cart totals
apps.about: Read-only HTTP adapters for django-cart pricing, checked against the pinned library. Includes PostgreSQL, queueing, transfer and JSON; no Django deployment score.
apps.seed: 4,096 or 65,536 carts, 32 price/quantity lines each; rotating IDs and mixed discount kinds.
apps.measurement_note: 2026-10-19 paired run: each server, PostgreSQL and client gets four CPU cores. SQL variants aggregate in PostgreSQL. Batch variants collect up to 256 requests for 1 ms, fetch fresh rows in one SQL query, then compute on CPU or CUDA. GPU-single is the same GPU path without coalescing; no resident input cache. Three repetitions per point.

apps.title: django-cart line scaling
apps.about: The same cart total with 32, 128, 512 or 2,048 lines. Live HTTP and PostgreSQL; exact upstream Decimal checks. This measures read-only adapters to the pricing library.
apps.seed: Fixed 4,096 carts: 131,072 to 8,388,608 line rows. Each HTTP request returns one cart total.
apps.measurement_note: 2026-10-19: nine implementations, 16/256 clients, three repetitions. Each server, PostgreSQL and client gets four CPU cores. Batch variants share one SQL worker, collect up to 256 requests for 1 ms, and fetch fresh rows. CUDA includes allocation, upload and download. Cooperative CUDA uses 32 threads per cart; parallel CPU uses four Rayon workers. SQL baselines use 16 connections. No resident input cache. These CUDA mappings are not an optimal-GPU bound.
